reviewed_by: Claude Code, PR 1 of the Butler home worker design at the operator's request
reason: Live Core showed Butler questions taking 4-50 minutes because every transaction of a project's worker runs one at a time and Apple Bug Bounty held 45-84 concurrent turns. This PR adds the foundation for running Butler on its own worker: a reserved __nebula_butler__ project hidden from store listings, counts, overview, search and CRUD edits; observer_reads(), which lets only the home project's worker read other projects' committed rows while row locks and writes stay fenced to its own project; and a butler.home/v1 release feature that gates admission, plus a capacity-retirement exemption. Selected: the new scope suite (observer reads, write and lock fencing, refusal on other workers, hidden listings, search and CRUD guards, admission gate), the existing execution-scope suite (SELECT branch changed), mixed-release idle retirement and admission retry/capacity (auto-admission changed), runtime worker features and bundle tests (release feature list changed), and the deployer protocol and simulation bundle tests (manifest features).
exclusions: tests/v3/test_execution_locks.py::test_handoff_waits_for_an_in_flight_source_write[postgresql] fails identically on unmodified origin/main a50eecc (3/3 runs locally), so test_execution_locks.py is not selected; its other cases passed with this change. No UI, settings or operator-visible behaviour changes: nothing creates the home project yet, so frontend and Playwright selections are empty and LAN validation does not apply. PostgreSQL cases skip without NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL in CI; all selected suites passed locally against the staging postgres:16 container (nebula_pytest database).
